sentences.text: Two retirees with the same balance, the same withdrawals and the same average return.
One ran out of money in 1991.
So what decided it?
It is January 1966.
The first retiree starts with $1 million, measured in 1966 dollars.
Their money is the water in this glass tank.
In the first year, the retiree withdraws 4% of the starting balance.
That is $40,000, in 1966 dollars.
After that, the withdrawal rises each year with the previous year's inflation, so it always buys the same groceries.
The tap is that withdrawal, and it widens as prices rise.
The plan runs for 30 years, from 1966 through 1995.
Each stone on this road is one year's return; a losing year sinks below the road.
As the tank passes each stone, the water rises or falls with that year.
Now meet the second retiree.
The mirror retiree lives through the exact same 30 annual returns, but in reverse order.
The return of 1995 arrives first, and the return of 1966 arrives last.
So the mirror tank walks the same road, the other way.
After inflation, stocks and bonds both lose money in 1973 and 1974.
In 1974 alone, the portfolio loses 14.7%, while prices rise 12.3%.
In 1966 dollars, the 1966 retiree ends 1974 with $461,000.
The mirror retiree, same year, same withdrawals: $1.27 million, also in 1966 dollars.
